items.difficulty_reason: The statement is the pointed refinement of the base change lemma for one step devissages: the primed data must realise a one step devissage of F'/X'/S' at the specific closed point x' over x, not merely over the base point (statement lines 930-938). The whole substance is that the extra hypothesis kappa(s) = kappa(s') makes the base change maps induce isomorphisms X'_{s'} = X_s, Z'_{s'} = Z_s and Y'_{s'} = Y_s, which is exactly what conditions (1)-(4) of the at-a-point definition test; without the residue-field hypothesis this transport fails (proof lines 945-950). The author carries the whole argument in five lines by quoting the over-s' lemma and the definition, so the difficulty is the localisation bookkeeping and not a new construction: H2.
